title: Volume One
review: Listen to this on the flight home from SF for the first time. After going to the concert nothing much compares to how Zooey Deschanel voice sounds in person. Actually such a great concert and her voice is so good. The album is a great example of her voice, and the guitar is also good. To me this is a pre Clairo type of music with great vocals and supporting background production.
genre: Indie Pop (or Alternative Country / Indie Folk)

title: Man on the Moon: The End of Day
review: Great album with so many great hit on it. Also the album has a lot of cohesion to it and I feel like Cudi put a lot of feeling into the album. Cudi Zone probably favorite on the album, but honestly so many great tracks on the album. Definitely an album to listen to front to back.

title: Swimmer
review: Bro this is a new top ten album for me just banger after banger. Godly voice followed with a synth pop style of music that is actually just so fire Idk even how to say it. They need to make more music like bro why do you stop after releasing such a banger of an album. Runner on the album might come close to the song of the summer, Anna went off on this song. Oh also how I found this album was by watching a recommendation video by Ken Jennings during a commerial break of jeopardy when he answers quesitons from the audience.

title: Summer's Over
review: Pretty good album only songs I really remember off the alum are Better in the Dark, Summer's Over, and Jump the Turnstile which are all pretty good tracks but they still i think the concert turned me off to her a little. Like maybe TV girl is carrying on this album and I don't know. I mean she has a great voice but idk if we see more bangs out of her.

title: Melt My Eyez See Your Future
review: Definity the best Denzel Curry album I have listen to so far. Also I love the jazz version of some of the songs specifically X-Wing. Denzel Curry is very underrated and deserves actually be known about. Jackson is the person that put me onto this album originally in high school. I think bro might have had like over 300 scrobbles on this album.

title: Where we’ve been, Where we go from here
review: I listened to the album originally when is came out. Came across it by accident but I also think Sidney talked about it to me. Pretty good indie rock album it has the feeling of almost every indie rock album where they are trying really hard but not quite making a great album. The best songs on the album are Crimson to Chrome, Get Numb To It!, and the Weird Fishes cover. Surprised the band has not made it bigger, although they are playing in Atlanta so maybe I will go.

title: Imaginal Disk
review: Bro this album is actually godly. This is a top 10 album for me like why is there not more music like this in the world. The vocals go crazy and the production is so good, and they just put banger after banger on the album. Was listening to this again on the way to SF and it is a album to close your eyes to and just enjoy every second. The glaze goes crazy. The stretch from Killing time to Fear, Sex is probably the best on the album but a well rounded album and makes me want to find more synth pop.

title: Wish You Were Here
review: Idk if this even counts as a listen but on the way back to ATL from SF I disassociated and slept but randomly I would wake up to Shine on you Crazy Dimond and be blessed with some of the most magical music ever made.

title: Reality Awaits
review: I am writing this review so late but I don't care because I wrote down every though I had of each song and sent it to Noah so whatever. I had a feeling this album would suck and it lived up to the amount of suck. Bro my are we using auto tune so much, I have listened to all of the other albums and they are great, WHY!! I will give a lot of credit Fabrizio Moretti bro is just great a drums but it gets drown out by the worst vocial performance by a gernational talent in Julian Casablancas. There were still some good tracks though if we got rid of auto tune, like Going Shopping and Going to Babble on.

title: From Chaos
review: Mid, very much embarrassing the 2000s style of alternative rock with really a lack of singing and more just high volume talking over some drums and guitars. I will say it does have one of my favorite songs of all time on it -- Amber. What a godly song but the rest of the album does not match up to it. Some other decent songs including Champagne, but idk it feels like it is mostly all the same song sometimes.

title: Section.80
review: I love this album so much actually had me bumping all summer. The starting track really makes it feel like a whole and gives it continues cohesion of this around the campfire in the city. Actually taken me to another place when I listen to this album. Also hol'up might be one of my favorite tracks by Kendrick idk why it is just so good and i love listening to it. We listened to this album on the way to Yosemite and actually just started singing to the bangers on it.

title: AM
review: Yeah it is a good album, there is not much to be said here not. I feel like some people would take a bullet for Arctic Monkeys but that is not me. Lucas and Mia are definitely those people, but I am not getting all of the hype like yeah good songs but nothing is really like this might be the greatest album of  the 2010s. Might be a little bit of hype here.

title: Second Helping
review: The second best Skynyrd album in my opinion.  The guitar and vocals are so good and just has a lot of songs that are just classic rock song. Sweet Home Alabama is honestly a skip for me though, one of the most overplayed songs of all time. There is no way that Alabama needs to be glazed. On the other hand I Need You if a song I don't here enough and deserves to be on every dad playlist ever made.
